items.title: Pollinator functional group responses to urban land cover in Merseyside, UK
items.summary: An exploratory modelling study found that predicted habitat suitability for bee and hoverfly functional groups varied across urban land cover, including some densely developed areas.
items.why: Offers a UK example for discussing functional traits, species distribution models and the limits of habitat predictions.

items.title: The audience shapes the information content of the honey bee waggle dance
items.summary: Honey bees communicated food direction and distance less precisely when suitable dance followers were scarce, showing that the audience influences the signal.
items.why: An accessible update to animal communication teaching and a good example of testing a familiar biological explanation.

items.title: Limited thermal tolerance in tropical insects and its genomic signature
items.summary: Measurements across approximately 2,300 tropical insect species revealed restricted scope for lowland communities to increase heat tolerance, alongside strong differences among insect lineages.
items.why: Links physiological limits, evolutionary relationships and climate-change vulnerability in a broad comparative study.

items.title: Biocontrol potential of Metarhizium spp. against Myzus persicae and beet mild yellowing virus in the post-neonicotinoid era
items.summary: Controlled experiments found that Metarhizium isolates killed aphids and that fungal colonisation of sugar beet was associated with reduced beet mild yellowing virus loads.
items.why: Provides a case study in fungal biocontrol while inviting discussion of strain effects and the evidence needed before field application.

items.title: Mosquito–capsid interactions contribute to flavivirus vector specificity
items.summary: The study identified molecular interactions within mosquitoes that help explain why particular mosquito species differ in their compatibility with flaviviruses.
items.why: Connects insect physiology to vector competence and shows why vector–pathogen relationships require species-specific evidence.
